summary.coverage: Both outlets are UK news organisations and cover the launch as a consumer product. The BBC reports a week of hands-on use and finds it helpful but awkward, while the Guardian focuses on tasks like Christmas shopping.

stories.headline: Amazon agreed to acquire AI startup Decart's chip optimisation software and hire its founders, in a deal reported at $7.5 billion.

summary.headline: Amazon agreed to acquire AI startup Decart's chip optimisation software and hire its founders, in a deal reported at $7.5 billion.
summary.coverage: Most outlets, including CNBC, the Financial Times and TechCrunch, report the deal as a business move that could help AWS compete with Nvidia on computing power. The Economic Times places it in a wider pattern of tech giants buying AI talent, while TechCrunch is the most upbeat. Ars Technica's headline in the set is about a different Amazon story, on hackers' AI agents.

rising.title: Ebony-Vinyl/dsh-our-free-model
rising.what: A Chinese-language plugin for the dsh tool that claims to give free access to several hosted models with no sign-up or API key.
rising.why: Someone curious about free hosted models might look at it, though the description's claims about free, unlimited access are unverified.

rising.title: EL4CTEO/fast-anything
rising.what: A toolkit for finding slow code in Python, Node or Ruby apps and porting only those hot functions to Rust with a coding agent.
rising.why: Developers wanting speedups without a full rewrite could use it, and it checks that ported functions behave the same as the originals.

rising.title: erkamyaman/rust-anything
rising.what: A set of agent skills for migrating whole applications from TypeScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby or Java into Rust, one piece at a time.
rising.why: Teams considering a language migration could use it to rewrite code incrementally while checking against recorded original behavior.

rising.title: affaan-m/ECC
rising.what: A performance and safety toolkit of skills, memory and rules for coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex.
rising.why: Someone using AI coding agents could reuse its configuration to make those agents faster, safer and more consistent.

rising.title: yetone/magpie
rising.what: A macOS menu bar app that routes coding agents like Codex and Claude Code to other model providers.
rising.why: Interests people who want to run Claude Code or Codex against models such as DeepSeek or Kimi.

rising.title: Graphify-Labs/graphify
rising.what: A tool that turns a codebase, its docs, schemas and PDFs into a searchable knowledge graph.
rising.why: Lets coding agents like Claude Code query how a project fits together without a vector store.

rising.title: NousResearch/hermes-agent
rising.what: An AI agent project described as one that grows with its user over time.
rising.why: The description is thin; it may appeal to people interested in long-running personal agents.

rising.title: stablyai/orca
rising.what: A desktop, mobile and remote app for running a fleet of coding bots on your own subscriptions.
rising.why: Relevant to people who run several Claude Code or Codex agents at once and want one control surface.

rising.title: JuliusBrussee/caveman
rising.what: A skill and local proxy that makes coding agents write shorter answers and receive smaller tool output.
rising.why: Aimed at people who want to cut token use when running coding agents, with originals recoverable.

rising.title: tt-a1i/archify
rising.what: A skill that turns ideas, plans or codebases into interactive architecture diagrams for coding agents.
rising.why: Useful for developers who want agents to generate visual diagrams of their designs.

rising.title: thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini
rising.what: A small mixture-of-experts vision-language model from Thinking Machines, distributed in Transformers format at 8-bit precision.
rising.why: Those following new open model releases may want to test it, and its description gives few further details.

rising.title: unsloth/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF
rising.what: A GGUF-format version of the Inkling-2-Mini mixture-of-experts vision-language model, prepared by Unsloth for local use.
rising.why: People wanting to run this small model locally on their own hardware could use this packaged version.

rising.title: inworld/voice-isolator
rising.what: A model that isolates a single voice from background noise in 48 kHz audio.
rising.why: Useful for anyone cleaning up speech recordings or building voice pipelines.

rising.title: tencent/Hy4-flash
rising.what: A Tencent model named Hy4-flash that handles images with text and generates text, built on the Transformers library.
rising.why: Someone following AI may care because it is a new open multimodal model from a major Chinese tech company; the description gives no further details.

rising.title: AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-GGUF
rising.what: A quantized GGUF build of an image-text model, with an uncensored LoRA adapter, for llama.cpp.
rising.why: Of interest to local-model users who want to run a vision-language model on their own hardware.

rising.title: JCisHERE/wan2-2-i2v-v3
rising.what: A Gradio demo space for an image-to-video model called wan2-2-i2v-v3, exposed as an MCP server.
rising.why: Anyone wanting to try image-to-video generation, or connect it to an agent through MCP, could use it, though little is known beyond the tags.

rising.title: MiniMaxAI/minimax-h3-image
rising.what: A Gradio demo Space from MiniMax for image generation or handling; the description is empty.
rising.why: Little is known beyond the name and Gradio tag; it may let people try a MiniMax image model.

rising.title: huggingface/moe-blogpost
rising.what: A Hugging Face Space packaged as a Docker container, apparently about mixture-of-experts models.
rising.why: The description says nothing beyond its name and tag; little is known about what it does.

rising.title: Vyber07/cyber-security
rising.what: A dataset described as a broad cybersecurity knowledge base for training AI, covering offensive and defensive security topics.
rising.why: Researchers building security-focused AI models could find it useful, though the description gives little detail on its contents or quality.

rising.title: Angais/pixel-art-atlas-1.4m
rising.what: A dataset of 1.4 million synthetic 16x16 pixel art game sprites with English captions.
rising.why: Could interest people training small image models or building game asset pipelines.

rising.title: nvidia/USDCraft-10K
rising.what: A dataset of 10,000 simulation-ready articulated 3D assets in OpenUSD format, generated with a language model.
rising.why: Relevant to robotics and simulation researchers who need physically usable 3D objects.

rising.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
rising.what: A paper describing an autoregressive diffusion Mamba model that generates long, controllable humanoid motion in real time.
rising.why: Those interested in animation or humanoid robot control could care, as it targets responding to changing instructions while moving.

rising.title: cmHC: Balancing Stream Mixing in Hyper-Connections via Geometric Contraction
rising.what: A paper proposing a way to keep mixing of residual streams in hyper-connections stable by constraining it geometrically.
rising.why: Researchers working on training stability for large dense and mixture-of-experts models would be the main audience.

rising.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
rising.what: A study of how frontier multimodal models can act as robot controllers when given the right tool and visual interfaces.
rising.why: Relevant to readers following whether general models can directly control robots in manipulation tasks.

rising.title: Non-penetrating World Models
rising.what: A benchmark and lightweight add-on that uses frozen diffusion transformer features to stop objects passing through each other in video world models.
rising.why: Relevant to people following physical realism and interactive world models.

rising.title: 3AGameFactory-Motion: Agentic Rigging and Reliable Complex Motion Generation for Diverse 3D Assets
rising.what: A benchmark and agent framework that writes skeleton and motion programs to rig 3D assets and generate their motion.
rising.why: Of interest to people tracking how LLM agents are applied to 3D animation.

press_not_builders.headline: The US Commerce Department added Megaspeed, a Southeast Asian chip firm linked to an Nvidia scandal, to its trade blacklist.
Oregon and Virginia sued SpaceX, alleging its Grok AI generated sexualized deepfake images and violated state consumer protection laws.
Mathematician Levent Alpöge, using Anthropic's Claude, claims a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and two groups say they verified it.
US prosecutors say a former OpenAI engineer secretly recorded dozens of confidential meetings using a hidden recorder and Codex.
